title: How We Almost Got Rid of Polio
summary: Josh and Chuck explore the history of polio, from its ancient origins and early-20th-century epidemics to the development of the Salk inactivated vaccine (IPV) and the Sabin oral vaccine (OPV), the Dutch cost-saving cell culture work, and the current push toward eradication, including setbacks such as the CIA fake vaccination campaign. The episode also includes a book pre-order plug, a note on a recent Selects rerun about viruses, and a listener mail correction about the Byzantine Empire.
topics: Netherlands monkey kidney cell vaccine production
Stuff You Should Know book preorder

segments.title: Book preorder plug and episode opening
segments.summary: The hosts promote the upcoming Stuff You Should Know book and its preorder gift, then introduce the episode on polio as a disease nearing eradication, with endemic cases remaining in only a few countries.
topics: Stuff You Should Know book preorder

segments.title: Polio virus, transmission and paralytic disease
segments.summary: The hosts distinguish poliovirus (the infection) from polio (the disease), explain fecal and saliva transmission, note that most infections are asymptomatic, and describe how a small share of cases reach the central nervous system and cause paralysis, with no cure and treatment limited to supportive care such as the iron lung.

segments.title: Pop culture aside and Selects reference
segments.summary: Chuck and Josh joke about iron lungs in film, including The Big Lebowski and The Outsiders, and Josh mentions a recent Selects episode on viruses, Virus Talk, from March 2020.

segments.title: Ancient history and early 20th-century epidemics
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the difficulty of tracing polio's origins, possible ancient evidence in Egyptian mummies, and how improved sanitation in the early twentieth century left populations unexposed, producing large outbreaks that frightened parents, especially in the US.

segments.title: March of Dimes and Jonas Salk's vaccine
segments.summary: The hosts describe the outbreaks' impact on American public life, the March of Dimes founded by Franklin Roosevelt that funded research, and Jonas Salk's inactivated vaccine, which he chose not to patent. Earlier researchers and the deadly Brody and Colmer vaccine trial are also mentioned.

segments.title: Ad break
segments.summary: Mid-episode break before the next segment.

segments.title: Salk field trial and the Polio Pioneers
segments.summary: The hosts cover the 1954 vaccine rollout to a million children called Polio Pioneers, the double-blind test, and the group of about two hundred thousand given a live, non-inactivated vaccine, in which forty thousand developed polio and ten died. The U.S. government temporarily suspended vaccination programs, though parents largely kept vaccinating.

segments.title: Sabin oral vaccine and the Cutter incident
segments.summary: Albert Sabin's live oral polio vaccine (OPV) on sugar cubes is described, with its low cost, testing in the Soviet Union, and wide use in the US from the early 1960s. The Cutter incident, where about two thousand children received active polio, undermined Salk's vaccine and helped OPV become the standard. The three poliovirus types are covered.

segments.title: Risks of live vaccine and Dutch cost reduction
segments.summary: The hosts explain vaccine-associated paralytic polio, the risk that the live strain mutates in the gut, and the advantage of OPV in spreading immunity in poor-sanitation areas. They then describe the Netherlands researchers who grew polio on monkey kidney cells on plastic beads, cutting the need for thousands of rhesus monkeys and making IPV cheaper.

segments.title: Eradication progress and the CIA fake vaccination campaign
segments.summary: The hosts explain the combined IPV and OPV strategy, the 2015 declaration that type two poliovirus was eradicated, the type three status, the difference between eradication and elimination, and case counts falling from 350,000 to 22 in 2017. They then describe how a CIA fake hepatitis C vaccination campaign used in the bin Laden search damaged trust and set back polio eradication in Nigeria, Afghanistan and Pakistan.

segments.title: Wrap-up
segments.summary: The hosts close the polio discussion, noting that eradication may take another twenty years.

segments.title: Listener mail on the Byzantine Empire
segments.summary: Listener Conrad corrects an earlier claim in the flamethrower episode about the Byzantines being Turks, explaining they were Greek-speaking heirs of the Roman Empire who were overthrown by the Ottoman Turks in 1453.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts thank listeners for mail and remind them how to send listener mail, then sign off.
